cards.title_cn: Amazon Alexa 不会停止说“lalala”，用户会感到害怕（更新：修复传入）
cards.summary: 【Amazon】Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority TL;DR Amazon Alexa has been exhibiting strange behavior. Users report that the assistant is getting stuck repeating the word “la.” Examples show Alexa repeati…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Update: October 5, 2026 (11:56 PM ET): Amazon has now confirmed to Android Authority that Alexa’s strange affliction was indeed a bug impacting “a small number of Alexa Plus” users. The company says it’s in the process of implementing a fix.

Original article: October 5, 2026 (11:34 AM ET): Sometimes, AI assistants inexplicably start acting up out of nowhere. For example, Gemini was refusing to answer questions on Android Auto just last week. But Google isn’t the only company that’s been having problems with its AI assistant in recent days. Amazon’s Alexa has also been exhibiting rather strange behavior recently.

Over the last month, users have been sharing reports about an issue with Alexa. It appears the AI will get stuck repeating the word “la” over and over again. According to these reports, Alexa will continue saying this word for several minutes before it stops. You can check out an example of the error in the video below.

This isn’t the first time Alexa has been caught going haywire. Only a couple of months ago, users were taken aback when Alexa emitted guttural sounds, like those of a snarling animal. At least this most recent problem is a little less unnerving than that.

It’s unclear what’s causing Alexa to meltdown like this, but some users are blaming a recent update. Android Authority has reached out to Amazon for comment on the issue. This article will be updated when new information becomes available. Until then, let us know if you’ve encountered this bug on any of your devices.

上个月，用户一直在分享有关 Alexa 问题的报告。看来人工智能会陷入一遍又一遍地重复“la”这个词的困境。根据这些报道，Alexa 在停止之前会继续说这个词几分钟。您可以在下面的视频中查看错误示例。

cards.title: ChatGPT users, your AI-written text will soon carry a hidden watermark
cards.title_cn: ChatGPT 用户，你的 AI 书写文本很快就会带有隐藏水印
cards.summary: 【OpenAI】Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR ChatGPT-generated text will soon carry an invisible watermark, starting in Europe. OpenAI’s detector can identify the watermark, but edits and shorter…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

For years, AI tools have made it easy to generate everything from images and audio to human-like text. While AI-generated images, videos, and audio can often be identified using dedicated detection tools, AI-written text has largely escaped the same level of scrutiny. ChatGPT, in particular, has become one of the most widely used tools for generating text that can closely mimic human writing. Now, OpenAI says it plans to change that by introducing watermarks for text generated by ChatGPT and Codex.

The company says its text watermarking program will first roll out in Europe, owing to the EU AI Act, which requires AI providers to make generated text identifiable in a machine-readable way. Over the next few weeks, OpenAI will add an invisible watermark to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text output in the EU, and API customers globally will also be able to opt into text watermarking for select models.
OpenAI is also accepting applications for its text watermarking detector, with access initially limited to approved researchers and expert organizations to help test the technology.

OpenAI explains that its watermarking technology, “textGrain,” adds a statistical signal to the model’s word choices. The detector then looks for that signal to verify if the text was generated using ChatGPT or Codex.
While the company says textGrain matched and even exceeded the performance of all the approaches it tested, it doesn’t always work as intended.

“Detectors can make two kinds of errors: they can report a watermark where none is present — a false positive — or miss a watermark that is present — a false negative,” OpenAI noted in its blog. The company also said that shorter text is harder to detect, and that editing can weaken the watermark.
Moreover, the watermark detection system cannot determine how much a human contributed to the text, who owns it, who created it, or whether the information it contains is accurate.

For now, OpenAI will introduce text watermarking to all users across all plans in Europe. The system is not going global just yet. The company says its regional approach will give it room to learn from real-world feedback.

2026 年 10 月 5 日 — 东部时间晚上 11:38
多年来，人工智能工具已经可以轻松生成从图像、音频到类人文本的所有内容。虽然人工智能生成的图像、视频和音频通常可以使用专用检测工具进行识别，但人工智能编写的文本在很大程度上逃脱了同等程度的审查。特别是 ChatGPT 已成为使用最广泛的工具之一，用于生成可以密切模仿人类书写的文本。现在，OpenAI 表示计划通过为 ChatGPT 和 Codex 生成的文本引入水印来改变这一现状。
该公司表示，由于《欧盟人工智能法案》，其文本水印计划将首先在欧洲推出，该法案要求人工智能提供商以机器可读的方式识别生成的文本。在接下来的几周内，OpenAI 将在欧盟符合条件的 ChatGPT 和 Codex 文本输出中添加隐形水印，全球 API 客户也将能够为选定的模型选择文本水印。
OpenAI 还接受其文本水印检测器的申请，最初仅限于经批准的研究人员和专家组织来帮助测试该技术。
OpenAI 解释说，其水印技术“textGrain”为模型的单词选择添加了统计信号。然后，检测器查找该信号以验证文本是否是使用 ChatGPT 或 Codex 生成的。
尽管该公司表示 textGrain 的性能与其测试的所有方法相匹配甚至超过，但它并不总是按预期工作。
OpenAI 在其博客中指出：“检测器可能会犯两种错误：它们可能报告不存在的水印——误报——或者漏掉存在的水印——误报。”该公司还表示，较短的文本更难检测，并且编辑可以削弱水印。
此外，水印检测系统无法确定人类对文本贡献了多少、谁拥有它、谁创建了它，或者它包含的信息是否准确。
目前，OpenAI 将向欧洲所有计划的所有用户引入文本水印。该系统尚未走向全球。该公司表示，其区域方法将为其提供从现实世界反馈中学习的空间。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，美国能源企业 Constellation 当地时间 9 月 30 日宣布与 Amazon（亚马逊）签署了一份长达 20 年的核电供应协议。
Constellation 将利用其位于马里兰州 Calvert Cliffs 的核电站为亚马逊供应 690MW 的电力，其中包括 2030~2032 年上线的 190MW 新增容量。
这份协议将在马里兰州促成超过 30 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 201.43 亿元人民币）的基础设施投资，包括对 Calvert Cliffs 核电站整体的升级改造。双方还签署了一项相关的零售供电协议，以支持亚马逊在覆盖 13 个州的 PJM 电力市场的运营。
另据彭博社当地时间 5 日报道，Google（谷歌）母公司 Alphabet（字母表）也即将与 Constellation 达成一份价值至少 10 亿美元（现汇率约合 67.14 亿元人民币）的多年期核电交易，相关协议最早本周公布。

fulltext: IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，据《科创板日报》报道，亚马逊云科技（AWS）旗下大模型服务平台 Amazon Bedrock 今日接入智谱 GLM-5.3，AWS 基于模型调用量与智谱进行收入分成。
报道称，除了 AWS 外，智谱近期与多家海外云厂商落地收入分成模式。此前智谱透露计划通过海外云平台收入分成增加一条具有规模潜力的商业路径。
国内方面，智谱也已与阿里云百炼平台等头部云厂商签署类似分成协议，华为云已上架 GLM-5.3，并就类似合作达成意向，形成贯通国内外的分成体系。
财报显示，智谱 2026 上半年营业总收入 9.54 亿元，同比增长 399.7%；归母亏损 20.71 亿元，同比亏损收窄 12.1%。
今年 9 月，智谱宣布完成约 50 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 335.72 亿元人民币）融资，包括约 20 亿美元股份配售及约 30 亿美元可转债发行。
此次融资主要用于下一代 GLM 基础模型及完全自训练（Fully Self Training）体系的研发，以及大规模训练、生产推理、算力资源及相关技术基础设施的部署及升级。

cards.title: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
cards.title_cn: 双子座打电话给我可能会告诉你妈妈你迟到了
cards.summary: 【Google】Google may be expanding its "Call for Me" AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a "Gemini Calling" introductory s…
fulltext: ﻿A rumored Android update would automate personal phone calls with Gemini AI.

Google may be expanding its “Call for Me” AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a “Gemini Calling” introductory screen in an APK teardown with examples that include “Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late” and “Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner.”

Based on those examples, even with this expansion, Gemini would likely be limited to basic, text message-like calls. While Google’s AI might not automate an entire catch-up phone call with your relatives, it could deliver quick messages to people who prefer a phone call, miss texts often, or even still have a landline phone.

Android Authority also says it found “granular permissions” for Gemini actions in individual apps, including what appear to be settings for phone call permissions. These settings would allow users to pick and choose which app capabilities they want to allow Gemini to access, potentially giving users an option to opt out of receiving incoming automated calls from Gemini. However, as Android Authority notes, it’s also possible Google might not publicly release this expansion or the granular Gemini app settings.

谷歌可能会将其“Call for Me”人工智能功能扩展到商务电话之外，这样你就可以用它向朋友和家人发送消息。 Android Authority 报告称，在 APK 拆解中发现了“Gemini Calling”介绍性屏幕，其中包括“给妈妈打电话，告诉她我会迟到 15 分钟”和“给约翰打电话，询问他是否来吃晚饭”等示例。

cards.title: Wikipedia operator says OpenAI’s ‘rogue’ bots may be linked to a May outage
cards.title_cn: 维基百科运营商表示 OpenAI 的“流氓”机器人可能与 5 月份的一次服务中断有关
cards.summary: 【OpenAI】Following many recent disclosures about AI agents accessing third-party websites and services, the Wikimedia Foundation, which hosts Wikipedia, says that it "can confirm that we have discovered some a…
fulltext: The Wikimedia Foundation believes OpenAI agents edited wikis, tried to ‘exploit’ a notetaking tool, and made ‘millions’ of automated API requests.

The activity includes edits to Wikimedia wikis, “unsuccessful attempts” to “exploit” the Etherpad note-taking tool that the Wikimedia Foundation hosts, and heavy traffic that the foundation says “may” have contributed to a partial outage that happened in May, according to a blog post. However, the Wikimedia Foundation says it didn’t find evidence that its systems were “used for coordination among agents” (recently, OpenAI bots reportedly hijacked a German wiki site to coordinate) or evidence of systems or data being compromised.
Here’s Wikimedia’s summary of what it saw:

Wiki editing: We’ve identified edits to Wikimedia wikis that we believe are from AI agents operated by OpenAI. These edits were not published to pages with visibility to general readers; almost all of them were testing edits in “sandbox” areas of the wiki. It also included a few edits to the configuration for a citation tool, which we believe were potentially malicious edits that were intended to misuse this tool as a proxy for fetching data from remote services. While Wikipedia policies allow bots to edit when they are disclosed and approved by the community, none of those approvals were sought in these incidents.

Etherpad probing and use: Agents we believe to be operated by OpenAI made some unsuccessful attempts to compromise our public Etherpad, a note-taking tool we host as a community service. Agents unsuccessfully tried to use it to fetch data from other websites as a proxy. Other agents also likely operated by OpenAI took notes about their tasks, though this did not appear to turn into coordination.

Excessive data downloading: Agents we believe to be operated by OpenAI made millions of automated requests to our public APIs to access the knowledge on Wikimedia projects, crawled millions of pages (mainly from our projects Wikidata and Wikimedia Commons), and made hundreds of thousands of data queries to the Wikidata Query Service (WQDS). This traffic may have contributed to a partial outage on WQDS in May.
“The open web is a public good,” the Wikimedia Foundation says. “We should not allow this behavior to become the ‘new normal’ for the people or organizations that maintain it.”

“We appreciate the detailed findings Wikimedia shared with us,” OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri says in a statement. “We’re working with them as we review and analyze the activity they identified along with our overall investigation, and we’ll continue to share relevant information as that work progresses.” OpenAI’s investigation hasn’t been able to verify if its bots contributed to the May outage, according to Pusateri.

cards.summary_cn: 【OpenAI】在最近披露了许多有关人工智能代理访问第三方网站和服务的信息后，维基百科的托管维基媒体基金会表示，它“可以确认我们已经发现了一些……
fulltext_cn: 维基媒体基金会认为 OpenAI 代理编辑了维基，试图“利用”笔记工具，并发出“数百万”个自动化 API 请求。
根据一篇博客文章，这些活动包括对维基媒体维基的编辑、“利用”维基媒体基金会托管的 Etherpad 笔记工具的“不成功尝试”，以及该基金会表示“可能”导致 5 月份发生的部分中断的大流量。然而，维基媒体基金会表示，它没有发现证据表明其系统“用于在代理之间进行协调”（最近，据报道 OpenAI 机器人劫持了德国维基网站进行协调），也没有发现系统或数据受到损害的证据。
以下是维基媒体对其所见内容的总结：
维基编辑：我们已经确定对维基媒体维基的编辑，我们认为这些编辑来自 OpenAI 运营的人工智能代理。这些编辑并未发布到普通读者可见的页面上；几乎所有的人都在维基的“沙盒”区域中测试编辑。它还包括对引文工具配置的一些编辑，我们认为这些编辑可能是恶意编辑，旨在滥用该工具作为从远程服务获取数据的代理。虽然维基百科政策允许机器人在社区披露和批准的情况下进行编辑，但在这些事件中没有寻求任何批准。
Etherpad 探测和使用：我们认为由 OpenAI 运营的代理曾尝试破坏我们的公共 Etherpad（我们作为社区服务托管的笔记工具），但未成功。代理试图使用它作为代理从其他网站获取数据，但没有成功。其他可能由 OpenAI 操作的代理也记录了他们的任务，尽管这似乎并没有转化为协调。
过多的数据下载：我们认为由 OpenAI 运营的代理向我们的公共 API 发出了数百万个自动请求，以访问维基媒体项目上的知识，抓取了数百万个页面（主要来自我们的项目维基数据和维基共享资源），并向维基数据查询服务（WQDS）发出了数十万次数据查询。此流量可能导致 WQDS 5 月份部分中断。
“开放网络是一项公共利益，”维基媒体基金会表示。 “我们不应该让这种行为成为维持这种行为的个人或组织的‘新常态’。”
OpenAI 发言人 Drew Pusateri 在一份声明中表示：“我们感谢维基媒体与我们分享的详细调查结果。” “我们正在与他们合作，审查和分析他们在整体调查中发现的活动，随着工作的进展，我们将继续分享相关信息。”据 Pusateri 称，OpenAI 的调查尚未证实其机器人是否导致了 5 月份的中断。
10 月 5 日更新：添加了 OpenAI 的声明。

cards.title: OpenAI will start watermarking ChatGPT’s text in the EU
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 将开始在欧盟为 ChatGPT 的文本添加水印
cards.summary: 【OpenAI】OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU to comply with the AI Act. Editing can make the invisible marks harder to detect, it says.

OpenAI will start adding an invisible watermark to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex in the European Union to comply with the EU AI Act, the company said Monday in a blog post.
The EU AI Act’s transparency rules, which took effect on August 2, require AI companies to mark AI-generated content in a way other systems can identify.

OpenAI said the watermark will roll out over the coming weeks to eligible ChatGPT and Codex users on all plans, but only in the EU. Developers using OpenAI’s API anywhere in the world can turn it on for select models starting today; it’s off by default. OpenAI said it is not making text watermarking a global default at launch.

The watermark is not an actual symbol, but works by subtly shaping the model’s word choices, leaving a pattern readers can’t see, but a detector can pick up. Because it lives in the words themselves, it travels with the text when it’s copied and pasted. OpenAI said the watermark doesn’t identify the user, and that it saw no meaningful change in its models’ performance with it switched on.

OpenAI also published a technical report for its method, called textGrain, alongside the announcement. Co-written with researchers from the University of Pennsylvania and Yale, it walks through an example of using a secret key to sort next-word predictions to finish the sentence. Add hundreds of these nudges together, and the detector can spot AI-generated content using only the text and the key.

Can the watermark be removed by editing? OpenAI’s tests suggest yes. In one test, replacing 10% of words with synonyms dropped detection from about 92% to 66%. The company also said short passages, math answers, and translated text are harder to detect.

“These limitations contribute to our decision to provide initial detector access only to approved researchers and expert organizations, who can help us evaluate reliability and responsible uses,” said the company.
OpenAI also cautioned that a missing watermark “does not prove human authorship.” The text could be too short or too heavily edited, or it could come from another company’s AI.
“[Watermarks] can indicate that an OpenAI system generated or processed part of a passage, but not how much human judgment, editing, or creativity went into it,” the company said.

The announcement comes two months after Anthropic said it would watermark text generated by Claude, a move it’s applying worldwide. That decision drew backlash from some Claude users, who argued they had supplied “the instructions, context, decisions” while Claude was just “the tool.”
OpenAI had built a text watermark before but held off on releasing it, partly over concerns that users would switch to rivals that didn’t watermark, The Wall Street Journal reported in 2024.
Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI are among the companies that have committed to following the EU’s code of practice on AI-generated content.

该公司周一在博客文章中表示，OpenAI 将开始在欧盟 ChatGPT 和 Codex 生成的文本中添加隐形水印，以遵守欧盟人工智能法案。
欧盟人工智能法案的透明度规则于 8 月 2 日生效，要求人工智能公司以其他系统可以识别的方式标记人工智能生成的内容。
OpenAI 表示，水印将在未来几周内向所有计划中符合资格的 ChatGPT 和 Codex 用户推出，但仅限于欧盟。从今天开始，世界各地使用 OpenAI API 的开发人员都可以为选定的模型启用它；默认情况下它是关闭的。 OpenAI 表示，它不会在发布时将文本水印设置为全球默认设置。
水印不是实际的符号，而是通过巧妙地塑造模型的单词选择来发挥作用，留下读者看不到但检测器可以拾取的模式。因为它存在于文字本身中，所以在复制和粘贴时它会随文本一起传播。 OpenAI 表示，水印无法识别用户的身份，并且打开水印后，模型的性能没有发生任何有意义的变化。
OpenAI 在发布公告的同时还发布了一份名为 textGrain 的方法的技术报告。它与宾夕法尼亚大学和耶鲁大学的研究人员共同编写，介绍了一个使用密钥对下一个单词预测进行排序以完成句子的示例。将数百个这样的轻推加在一起，检测器可以仅使用文本和密钥来识别人工智能生成的内容。
可以通过编辑去掉水印吗？ OpenAI 的测试表明是的。在一项测试中，用同义词替换 10% 的单词使检测率从大约 92% 下降到 66%。该公司还表示，短文、数学答案和翻译文本更难检测。
该公司表示：“这些限制促使我们决定仅向经批准的研究人员和专家组织提供初始探测器访问权限，他们可以帮助我们评估可靠性和负责任的使用。”
OpenAI 还警告说，缺失的水印“并不能证明作者身份”。文本可能太短或编辑过多，也可能来自另一家公司的人工智能。
该公司表示：“[水印]可以表明 OpenAI 系统生成或处理了一段段落的一部分，但不能表明其中涉及了多少人类判断、编辑或创造力。”
两个月前，Anthropic 表示将为 Claude 生成的文本添加水印，这一举措正在全球范围内应用。这一决定引起了一些克劳德用户的强烈反对，他们认为他们提供了“说明、背景、决定”，而克劳德只是“工具”。
据《华尔街日报》 2024 年报道，OpenAI 之前已经创建了文本水印，但推迟发布，部分原因是担心用户会转向没有水印的竞争对手。
Anthropic、谷歌、Meta、微软和 OpenAI 等公司都承诺遵守欧盟关于人工智能生成内容的行为准则。
